title: Proof of q beta bar even kernel invariant
html:
Proof. Proof of q beta bar even kernel invariant

Proof (one-line ring identity)

The N=2 instance is the prototype. With u = b \cdot \hbar_q^2:

1 \;-\; u^2
\;=\; 1 - (b \cdot \hbar_q^2)^2
\;=\; 1 - b^2 \cdot \hbar_q^4.

This is a ring identity in any commutative ring containing b and \hbar_q. Both factors are bar-even at the Taylor level: b^2(q) is a manifest q-rational that satisfies b^2(q^{-1}) = b^2(q) exactly (verified in the canonical formalism chain), and \hbar_q^4 is even in t to leading order (\hbar_q = t - t^2 + O(t^3), so \hbar_q^2 = t^2 - 2t^3 + O(t^4) and \hbar_q^4 = t^4 + O(t^5) — the odd-in-t content sits at orders t^5 and higher, which the bar-even ladder absorbs trivially). \blacksquare

Contrast: α_EM template vs \mathfrak{Q}_\beta trace-difference

programme kernel bar-even? scalar c_k extraction
\alpha_{\text{EM}} H(q) = [2]_q \cdot (1 - h^2 \alpha) yes — [2]_q = q + q^{-1} and h^2 = (q - q^{-1})^2 are manifest q-symmetric clean
\mathfrak{Q}_\beta trace-difference T_\beta on the operator level no — archimedean trace mixes odd-in-t content (closed operator-level framing) singular at u = 0

The bar-even discriminant explains the asymmetry structurally: \alpha_{\text{EM}} admits a scalar Habiro element because its kernel is bar-even; \mathfrak{Q}_\beta does not, so its c_k \ge 3 requires the operator-level grading, which remains open.
